title: Lexeme latency bridge for multi-layer cache chargeback
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Teams need per-output (lexeme) visibility into latency and cost so they can understand the marginal effect of multi-layer caching (prefix cache, KV cache, local prefetch) and batching on end-to-end SLOs and unit economics. Current tracing surfaces request-level spans only; it is insufficient to attribute latency and cache chargebacks when a single streaming response interleaves cached prefixes, prefetched KV hits, and on-demand kernel execution.

Goal: Implement a lightweight "lexeme-latency-bridge" instrumentation that emits a stable per-lexeme identifier and three minimal timing hooks (enqueue, kernel_start, emit) that propagate through the runtime, batching layer, and metrics/log pipelines. The bridge will correlate lexeme-level events with cache-hit metadata (which cache layer and hit latency) and export an aggregated, queryable stream for billing and dashboarding without exploding cardinality.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Lexeme-level events emitted for >95% of streaming responses in the canary pool with no more than 3% p99 latency overhead on end-to-end requests.
2) Each lexeme event contains: lexeme_id, request_id, seq_index, model_version, kernel_tag, cache_layers_hit (list), enqueue_ts, kernel_start_ts, emit_ts.
3) Grafana dashboard showing lexeme-level median/p50/p95/p99 latency slices and per-cache-layer chargeback impact.
4) Aggregation pipeline that reduces cardinality: ability to materialize per-request rollups and sampled per-lexeme traces.
5) Billing pipeline shows delta in token-unit cost attributable to cache hits for two sample customers compared to baseline.
6) Automated tests and a staged rollout plan to Dedicated and Hosted with canary throttles and fallback to existing tracing if errors occur.
technical_notes:
Design constraints: cardinality explosion is the main risk. Strategy: emit compact lexeme events with tags that are high-cardinality only when sampled (e.g., full prompt hash) and otherwise rely on rollup keys (model_version, route, customer_tier). Use a 1% deterministic sample for full context traces (trace_id propagated) and a 100% lightweight event stream for metric rollups.

Instrumentation hooks:
- enqueue: when the lexeme enters the runtime queue (captures queue latency and prefetch hits).
- kernel_start: when model kernel begins executing for that lexeme (captures scheduling and preemption delays).
- emit: when the lexeme is sent to the network/stream buffer (captures actual emission latency and serialization time).

Cache correlation: annotate events with cache_layers_hit (e.g., [prefix_cache, kv_local, kv_remote]) and per-layer latency if available. KV prefetch/proactive hits will emit a prefetched flag to avoid double-charging.

Telemetry pipeline: push lightweight events to the existing ingestion topic (kafka://observability.lexeme_events.v2) with a compact Avro schema. A downstream Flink job will perform sessionization to assemble lexeme timelines and produce two outputs:
- rollup metrics (Prometheus-friendly aggregates with controlled labels)
- sampled spans exported to Jaeger/Tempo for deep debugging.

Backwards compatibility: if runtime cannot reliably emit kernel_start (older nodes), we fallback to best-effort derived kernel_start using enqueue + expected scheduling latency and mark as inferred in the event metadata.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (week 0-1): spec Avro schema and proto for lexeme_event; add hooks in runtime enqueue path and emission path; add cache_layer flagging in cache adapters. Link design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Lexeme+Latency+Bridge.
Phase 2 (week 2): implement kernel_start hook in kernel scheduler and wire lexeme_id propagation through batching and KV code paths. Add deterministic sampler (1%) that attaches full trace context.
Phase 3 (week 3): deploy to canary pool (10% traffic) and run load test with the synthetic streaming workload; measure overhead and cardinality.
Phase 4 (week 4): implement Flink sessionizer job to assemble timelines and produce Prometheus-friendly rollups; create Grafana dashboards and billing exporter to the cost pipeline.
Phase 5 (week 5): QA, docs, and staged rollout to hosted + Dedicated with rollback plan.

Implementation notes: prefer non-blocking logging to avoid tail latency amplification; all event emissions must be bounded by 200 microsecond budget per lexeme on the fast path.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for lexeme_id propagation across serialization boundaries.
- Integration test that simulates prefix cache hits and KV prefetch hits, verifying lexeme timelines include cache_layers_hit and correct latency deltas.
- Load test targeting canary nodes to measure p50/p95/p99 overhead and event ingestion throughput.
- Regression run against existing token-level billing reports to detect discrepancies >1%.
- Chaos test: simulate partial failure of Flink job and verify rollups still emitted from fallback aggregator.
rollout_plan: Canary 10% (canary pool) for 72h with automated SLO checks (error rate, tail latency, event ingestion lag). If SLOs hold, expand to 50% for 48h, then full rollout. Dedicated customers will be opted-in via feature flag and provided migration notes. Immediate rollback path: disable lexeme_event emission in runtime config and fall back to request-level tracing.
observability_queries: # Lexeme latency histogram aggregated by model and cache hits: sum(rate(lexeme_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, cache_layers_hit)
# Median emit-to-kernel_start across models: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(lexeme_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
# Fraction of lexemes with any cache hit: sum(rate(lexeme_events_total{cache_any=\"true\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(lexeme_events_total[5m]))
# Ingestion lag for lexeme stream: max(le_message_latency_seconds) by (cluster)
# Sampled span count vs full events: rate(lexeme_sampled_spans_total[5m]) / rate(lexeme_events_total[5m])
